findings.note: coast : ocean reads the same as ocean : coast — touching is mutual by definition
Nothing forces genre-first vs example-first; the mirrored order (Hamlet:tragedy::Hamilton:musical) reads equally well.
Device-then-effect vs effect-then-device is arbitrary; both directions are equally readable.
Could equally be written debut:entrance::retirement:bow; nothing in the words themselves fixes which column is 'performance act' vs 'career term' first.
Unclear which two words pair together at all, let alone their order; the grouping and direction are both guesses.

notes:
Fix set-touching-spaces' inherently symmetric relationship (requires new pair concept/grain, not just reordering) and add order-forcing cues to the three order-guessed sets via word/label edits.
- set-touching-spaces: Contiguity (coast:ocean paradigm) is symmetric by definition — wing:stage reads identically reversed, and reports also flag unclear pairing/grouping itself.
  Try: Replace with a different relationship id (e.g. dimensional-similarity, 'stream:river' paradigm) using part/whole stage pairs with a clear size or containment direction, such as apron:stage :: house:theater
  Or: Re-author using instrument-action or sequence stance instead of contiguity, keeping theater vocabulary but picking a relationship with inherent directionality (e.g. wing : entrance as 'space : action enabled there')
  Or: If keeping contiguity, switch paradigm to a whole-part contiguity that's asymmetric by convention (e.g. frame : picture) and find theater analogs where one term is clearly the container and the other the contained edge
- set-genre-example: Order between genre and example is arbitrary; Hamlet:tragedy::Hamilton:musical reads equally well.
  Try: Sharpen relationshipLabel to explicitly name direction, e.g. 'a kind of play, named — genre first, example second' so the fixed order is stated rather than inferred
  Or: Add a genre that has multiple well-known examples to bait the reader into needing the genre-first frame, e.g. keep tragedy:Hamlet but pick a musical example less genre-ambiguous, or reframe pairs as (genre, defining trait) instead of (genre, title) to remove reversibility
- set-tool-action: Tool-then-effect vs effect-then-tool order is arbitrary; both directions read equally.
  Try: Reword relationshipLabel to state direction explicitly, e.g. 'a stage tool, then the action it exists to perform' to anchor column order for the reader
  Or: Swap one pair's word choice to a tool name that cannot double as a verb/effect noun, reducing symmetry, e.g. replace 'trap door' pairing with a tool whose action name is clearly not swappable
- set-span-moments: Column order between performance-scale and career-scale terms is arbitrary; debut:entrance::retirement:bow reads equally.
  Try: Reorder pairs consistently as (career milestone, performance milestone) — debut:entrance :: retirement:bow — and rewrite label to state that order explicitly
  Or: Replace one pair to remove the near-synonym alternate-reading risk noted by adversarial solver, e.g. swap 'bow' for a word not synonymous with 'retirement' such as 'curtain call'

Editor blocks set-span-moments as order-ambiguous, confirmed by adversarial solver and test-player who both matched entrance:debut::curtain call:retirement instead of the intended scaling. Editor explicitly wants this set replaced. All other sets praised by editor as publishable and must be left untouched.
- set-span-moments: entrance/curtain call/debut/retirement can be validly cross-read as entrance:debut::curtain call:retirement (start-start, end-end) instead of the intended within-scale bracketing, making the order ambiguous.
  Try: Editor's directive: replace the set entirely with a new before-after pair-set that doesn't admit a start/end cross-reading (editor's leading fix — replace, not repair)
  Or: Choose two spans whose four terms are not each independently splittable into 'starts' and 'ends' categories, e.g. sunrise:sunset :: birth:death paired as (sunrise,sunset) and (birth,death) but where the words themselves don't read as a natural start-category and end-category across pairs
  Or: Pick a pair-scale combo where one word only makes sense paired with its own-scale partner (e.g. use a term with no career-arc equivalent, like 'blackout' instead of 'curtain call', which is stage-only and blocks the cross-scale swap)
Do not change: set-genre-example, set-tool-action, set-touching-spaces — these were approved.
